1.1.4:
Perfect timing feedback appears as you release the last mark. Each new exercise or retry starts with a clear sending display. In Settings → Input, choose how long to pause after your answer. Changing sending speed remembers your chosen spacing speed.

Progress now shows Listen and Send sessions together and includes six sending badges. The leaderboard shows your shared XP alongside your total XP. Turning sharing on applies to new results from then on.
1.1.3:
After hearing a Send prompt, you can switch apps, reconnect the paddle output or adjust speed, spacing, pitch and volume and keep sending. A slider change during playback lets the prompt finish. An interrupted answer is cleared before grading.

Keyboard paddles and VBand USB work while a Send slider is selected. The arrow keys still adjust the slider.
1.1.2:
Your sending highlights the next mark and shows how early, late, short or long your timing was. With a paddle, practise the gaps between letters and words. A perfectly timed transmission earns a burst of fireworks. With Reduce Motion enabled, the feedback is static.

The Listen first prompt fits long exercises without an inner scrollbar. Saved progress now shows when your changes have reached the website and keeps your sending playback preferences on this device.
1.1.1:
In Settings → Input, choose a pause of 0.5–15 seconds after your last mark, or wait for E or a single dit after grading. Under Key input → Paddles · keyboard, choose your own dot and dash characters and show or hide the on-screen buttons.

Your sending keeps its height while you key and review an answer. The Mac can read the website leaderboard. Uploads and private pairing require the website’s version 2 service.

After a manual upgrade from 1.1.0, Settings → Updates can install future signed updates. Automatic updates are off by default.
1.1.1-dev.2: Settings → Input lets you choose when the next sending signal plays. Set a pause from your last mark, or continue after grading with E or a single dit. Under Key input → Paddles, assign your own dot and dash characters and choose whether to show the on-screen paddles.
1.1.1-dev.1: The sending display keeps its height as you key and review an exercise. Saved progress contains all pairing controls. The Mac reads the website leaderboard and can pair once the website offers the new sync service. Configured builds install signed updates with Sparkle.
1.1.0:
Morse now includes the paddle engine. Choose Audio converter or VBand USB in Settings. One native keyer times the sidetone, the marks you send and paddle typing.

Your sending overlays your marks on the target timing. Correct exercises advance automatically. Send and Listen share speed, spacing, pitch and volume.

Practise offline and export progress from Saved progress. This Mac release keeps progress and scores on your Mac. The live leaderboard, private sync and recovery codes are unavailable.

Settings → Updates shows what’s new and checks for a Mac download. Automatic updates are off by default.
